question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC\) we have \(AB = 7,\) \(AC = 8,\) and \(BC = 9.\) Point \(D\) is on the circumscribed circle of the triangle so that \(\overline{AD}\) bisects \(\angle BAC.\) What is the value of \(\frac{AD}{CD}?\)

solutions.explanation:
The angle bisector gives a useful ratio on \(BC\), and the circle lets us connect that ratio to \(AD/CD\). Let \(E=AD\cap BC\). Because \(AD\) bisects the internal angle at \(A\), \(E\) lies between \(B\) and \(C\), with \(A,E,D\) in that order.

The angle-bisector theorem divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides, so
\[
\frac{BE}{EC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac78.
\]
Since \(BE+EC=9\), we get
\[
BE=\frac7{15}\cdot9=\frac{21}{5}.
\]
Now \(\angle ABE=\angle ABC=\angle ADC\), because the last two angles subtend the same arc \(AC\). Also, \(\angle BAE=\angle CAD\) by angle bisection. Thus \(\triangle ABE\sim\triangle ADC\), with corresponding vertices \(A\leftrightarrow A\), \(B\leftrightarrow D\), and \(E\leftrightarrow C\). Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{AB}{AD}=\frac{BE}{DC}.
\]
All these lengths are positive, so we may rearrange to obtain
\[
\frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{AB}{BE}
=\frac{7}{21/5}=\frac53.
\]
The answer is \(\frac53\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Angle-bisector ratio and similar triangles
